rawPrompt:
A moving particle has position $(x(t), y(t))$ at time $t$. The position of the particle at time $t=1$ is $(2,6)$, and the velocity vector at any time $t>0$ is given by $\left(1-\frac{1}{t^{2}}, 2+\frac{1}{t^{2}}\right)$.\\
(a) Find the acceleration vector at time $t=3$.\\
(b) Find the position of the particle at time $t=3$.\\
(c) For what time $t>0$ does the line tangent to the path of the particle at $(x(t), y(t))$ have a slope of 8 ?\\
(d) The particle approaches a line as $t \rightarrow \infty$. Find the slope of this line. Show the work that leads to your conclusion.\\
rawScoringGuide:
A moving particle has position \((x(t), y(t))\) at time \(t\). The position of the particle at time \(t=1\) is \((2,6)\) and the velocity vector at any time \(t>0\) is given by \(\left(1-\frac{1}{t^{2}}, 2+\frac{1}{t^{2}}\right)\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the acceleration vector at time \(t=3\).
\item[(b)] Find the position of the particle at time \(t=3\).
\item[(c)] For what time \(t>0\) does the line tangent to the path of the particle at \((x(t), y(t))\) have a slope of 8?
\item[(d)] The particle approaches a line as \(t \rightarrow \infty\). Find the slope of this line. Show the work that leads to your conclusion.
\item[(a)] acceleration vector \(=\left(x^{\prime \prime}(t), y^{\prime \prime}(t)\right)=\left(\frac{2}{t^{3}},-\frac{2}{t^{3}}\right)\)
\[
\left(x^{\prime \prime}(3), y^{\prime \prime}(3)\right)=\left(\frac{2}{27},-\frac{2}{27}\right)
\]
\item[(b)] \((x(t), y(t))=\left(t+\frac{1}{t}+C_{1}, 2 t-\frac{1}{t}+C_{2}\right)\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& (2,6)=(x(1), y(1))=\left(2+C_{1}, 1+C_{2}\right) \\
& C_{1}=0, C_{2}=5 \\
& (x(3), y(3))=\left(3+\frac{1}{3}, 6-\frac{1}{3}+5\right)=\left(\frac{10}{3}, \frac{32}{3}\right)
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2+\frac{1}{t^{2}}}{1-\frac{1}{t^{2}}}=8\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& 2+\frac{1}{t^{2}}=8\left(1-\frac{1}{t^{2}}\right) ; \quad t^{2}=\frac{9}{6} \\
& t=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)] \(\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{d y}{d x}=\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2+\frac{1}{t^{2}}}{1-\frac{1}{t^{2}}}=2\)
- or -
Since \(x(t) \rightarrow \infty\) as \(t \rightarrow \infty\), the slope of the line is
\[
\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{y(t)}{x(t)}=\lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2 t-\frac{1}{t}+5}{t+\frac{1}{t}}=2
\]
\end{itemize}
\(2 \begin{cases}1: & \text { components of acceleration } \\ & \text { vector as a function of } t \\ 1: & \text { acceleration vector at } t=3\end{cases}\)
\(3 \begin{cases}1: & \text { antidifferentiation } \\ 1: & \text { uses initial condition at } t=1 \\ 1: & \text { position at } t=3\end{cases}\)
Note: max 1/3 [1-0-0] if no constants of integration
\(2\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \quad \frac{d y}{d x}=8 \text { as equation in } t \\ 1: \text { solution for } t\end{array}\right.\)
\(2 \begin{cases}1: & \text { considers limit of } \frac{d y}{d x} \text { or } \frac{y(t)}{x(t)} \\ 1: & \text { answer }\end{cases}\)
Note: 0/2 if no consideration of limit
